source.description: Send the version's readable source, as people write it (not bundled or minified: lines under 1000 characters), because the admins read it before they decide. It is a CommonJS module that sets `module.exports.recipe = function (id, v, variant) { … return { meta, build } }`, requires only 'three', three's addons ('three/addons/…') and shared pieces by hash, and names every other asset by its BLAKE3 hash. A piece is readable source shared by recipes (a car kit, a battery pack), a document of kind 'piece' (list_docs, doc_at; made or changed with propose_doc_version, kind 'piece', whole { schema: 'piece/1', label, note, source }, a CommonJS module): a recipe names an accepted version of one by the BLAKE3 hash of its source, `require('<64 hex>')` (list_docs gives each piece's versions and their hashes), and the box reads it from play's files; a piece may require three.js and other pieces, at most 4 deep. A version keeps the pieces it was accepted with: a newer piece is a new version of the asset. Pieces may be proposed in the same intent as what uses them: a recipe or piece may require the hash of a piece version proposed in that intent, and one intent may carry several versions of one piece (each proposed in order, the next growing from the last); Accept keeps them first, in the order they require each other. play wraps it into the recipe file itself (the asset box's header, then the source, then the line naming this asset and its new version). The code runs only in the asset box, the sandboxed frame in the page, never on play's server. Start from the head's source (get_asset gives its hash, get_file its text). Every version has one: an imported version's is legacy's own code its recipe file was bundled from (the asset's library, each module marked by the file it came from), made again and checked against that file byte for byte. Every new version names its levels of detail on its card, `lod: { levels: 'declared' | 'derived' }` (propose_asset's `lod`; doc_edit's card field `card.lod`, carried on from the head where it has one): 'declared' where its source exports its own L1 and L2 as a plain literal, `module.exports.levels = [{ values: { … } }, …]`, each the same recipe built with those values (its params), else 'derived'; L0 is its build, L3 its picture.
